title: How Much of the Routine Reserve Standing is Kept Back
content:
How much of the routine reserve standing on a Keyturn Host Payout Account is kept back out of the sum freed turns on how the account settles and on how lately a routine reserve was taken.

1. **Where the account settles only when the host asks and a routine reserve was taken on it within the past week**, being 7 calendar days or fewer before that day, the whole routine reserve standing is kept back, that is 100 percent of it.
2. **Where the account settles only when the host asks and the newest routine reserve on it was taken more than a week but no more than a calendar quarter ago**, being more than 7 and no more than 92 calendar days before that day, half of the routine reserve standing is kept back, that is 50 percent of it.
3. **In every other case**, a quarter of the routine reserve standing is kept back, that is 25 percent of it.

The share is taken on the routine reserve standing, and the sum kept back is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## The two boundaries, from both sides

The age is counted in calendar days from the day of the newest routine reserve taken on the account up to that day. On an account settling only when the host asks: at 7 days the first case governs and the whole standing is kept back; at 8 days the second governs and half is kept back; at 92 days the second still governs; and at 93 days the third governs and a quarter is kept back.

## Where the account settles on another rhythm

The first two cases both require that the account settles only when the host asks. An account swept on any other rhythm falls to the third case however lately its newest routine reserve was taken, and a quarter of the routine reserve standing is kept back.

## On hypothetical figures

Where the routine reserve standing is 800.00 USD, the sum kept back is 800.00 USD in the first case, 400.00 USD in the second and 200.00 USD in the third.
